access_constraints_note: RESEARCH LIMITATION (read first): this session's WebSearch budget was already exhausted (200/200) by sibling agents before this agent ran, and the egress proxy blocked WebFetch to every domain tried (navy.mil, navwar.navy.mil, peoc4i.navy.mil, marcorsyscom.marines.mil, gao.gov, dvidshub.net, navysbir.com, defensescoop.com, breakingdefense.com, wikipedia, duckduckgo, bing). Bigdata.com was out of credits. The only working external channel was GitHub code search (text fragments only; file reads were denied outside the user's repo). Findings therefore rest on (a) GitHub-mirrored copies of official texts (an Engineering Duty Officer study guide dated 2026-06-05 that cites navy.mil/navwar.navy.mil/DVIDS/peoc4i.navy.mil URLs with publication dates; a MARADMIN/MCO citation portal; NAVADMIN and DoD budget-table mirrors), (b) sibling agents' JSON files in this scratchpad, and (c) clearly labeled general knowledge. Every URL below should be re-verified at the primary source before investment use; confidence levels reflect this indirection.

organizations.name: Assistant Secretary of the Navy (Research, Development and Acquisition)
organizations.portfolio: DON Service Acquisition Executive; charters PEOs/DRPMs and the new Portfolio Acquisition Executives (PAEs); Milestone Decision Authority for DON programs.
organizations.current_status_2026: FACT (via mirror of navy.mil release 2026-05-26): William F. Mahan named to perform the duties of ASN(RD&A) as senior acquisition executive; Jason L. Potter returned to Principal Civilian Deputy. VADM Seiko Okano serves as Principal Military Deputy (PMILDEP) and chairs Program Decision Meetings when delegated (late 2025-2026).
organizations.leader_title: Performing the Duties of ASN(RD&A) (William F. Mahan); PMILDEP (VADM Seiko Okano)
key_programs: Project Overmatch steering (Five Eyes arrangement chaired by PMILDEP)

organizations.name: Portfolio Acquisition Executive Mission Systems
organizations.portfolio: Central mission integrator for kill-chain closure across PEO C4I, PEO Digital, PEO IWS, PEO MLB, DRPM Overmatch, DRPM Long Range Naval Fires Office (LRNFO), DRPM Manpower IT Logistics ERP (MILE), the Minotaur program from NAVAIR PMA-290, and mission-system elements of NAVWAR, NAVSEA, NAVAIR and Marine Corps Systems Command.
organizations.current_status_2026: FACT (via mirror of navwar.navy.mil article 4483415 and navy.mil release 4483312, both 2026-05-11): publicly established 11 May 2026 with Jim Day as interim PAE. Answers the assignment question directly: PEO C4I and PEO Digital were NOT merged into one PEO in 2024-2026 on public evidence; instead both (plus PEO IWS and PEO MLB) were placed under a single portfolio executive. The DON release states roughly 70 percent of SYSCOM-associated functions/personnel will move into PAEs; PAEs have direct authority over program offices and associated technical, contracting and sustainment functions.
organizations.startup_relevance: HYPOTHESIS: as PAE staffs absorb contracting and technical functions, industry-engagement events will increasingly be run at the PAE level; monitor PAE Mission Systems industry days. As of Sept 2026 no PAE-level solicitation was found (public evidence insufficient).

organizations.parent: Chief of Naval Operations (Echelon II SYSCOM); acquisition support to ASN(RD&A)/PAEs

Enterprise: NAVWAR HQ (San Diego), three affiliated PEOs (C4I, Digital, MLB), Echelon III activities NIWC Atlantic, NIWC Pacific and NAVWAR Space Field Activity; more than 11,000 employees.

Doug Small as NAVWAR commander on 9 Aug 2024 with direct oversight of Project Overmatch (DVIDS 478261); by Nov 2025 she is cited as VADM and PMILDEP to ASN(RD&A). Identity of the NAVWAR commander as of Sept 2026: Public evidence insufficient. NAVWAR's PEOs now sit under PAE Mission Systems (11 May 2026); the study-guide source notes official NAVWAR pages still present the legacy enterprise structure unevenly.
organizations.leader_title: Commander, NAVWAR (Rear Adm.; current incumbent not verified this session)

Entry points found: NAVWAR Small Business Office mailbox (navwarsbo.fct@navy.mil, published on PEO C4I Small Business Fair notice), NAVWAR OSBP, Project Overmatch Prize Challenge (NAVWAR-run, historical), IWRP quarterly industry days.

organizations.current_status_2026: FACT (mirror of peoc4i.navy.mil tear sheets dated Jan 2026 / 2026-02-25 / 2025-01-31): PEO C4I continues as a distinct PEO with the office structure above; no merger with PEO Digital found. Governance now runs through PAE Mission Systems. Leader name as of 2026: Public evidence insufficient.

Black Pearl / The Forge DevSecOps (per sibling S09; Black Pearl is Navy DevSecOps platform; The Forge is NAVSEA/PEO IWS)

organizations.name: Direct Reporting Program Manager, Project Overmatch
organizations.parent: ASN(RD&A) via PAE Mission Systems (2026); historically NAVWAR-led
organizations.portfolio: Navy contribution to CJADC2: Naval Operational Architecture linking ships, submarines, aircraft, ground forces and uncrewed systems; modern data architectures, cloud-hosted analytics; Overmatch Software Armory for rapid fielding of commercial and custom code; Five Eyes coalition integration.
organizations.current_status_2026: FACT (DVIDS 514959, 2025-11-13; DVIDS 551112): Capt. Remil Capili is the public program manager; VADM Seiko Okano chairs the Five Eyes steering committee; a Project Arrangement with Australia, Canada, New Zealand and the UK embeds Cooperative Project Personnel in San Diego and a coalition lab supports continuous testing ahead of RIMPAC 2026. FACT (DVIDS 501030, 2025-06-18): Overmatch, NAVWAR, CDAO and DIU onboarded commercial AI/ML applications via the Open DAGIR pipeline so Fleet commanders could visualize readiness data (Maven Smart System) in weeks. Deployment history: network installed on three carrier strike groups by March 2024 (C4ISRNET 2024-03-06). Press (AOL/Tier 4, 2026-05-23) describes integrations tested at RIMPAC 2026 with spending planned through FY2029 and the effort 'far from being rolled out'. Most architecture and vendor details remain classified.
key_programs: Automated Test and Re-Test (congressional add FY2025)
organizations.startup_relevance: Highest-visibility Navy C2 buyer but least transparent: an Ocean Power Technologies FY2025 10-K (Tier 4) reports Overmatch participation with 'no definitive contract awards'. Realistic entry is via Open DAGIR/DIU/CDAO onboarding, IWRP prototypes, the OSA/RAISE pipeline, or as a subcontractor to integrators; direct awards to two-founder startups are unlikely near term (INFERENCE, HIGH).

organizations.name: Naval Information Warfare Center Pacific
organizations.portfolio: Research, development, prototyping, engineering, T&E, installation and sustainment for information-warfare capabilities; hosts the Overmatch Software Armory (niwcpacific.navy.mil/Technology/Overmatch-Software-Armory); San Diego. Contracting office DODAAC N66001 (general knowledge; verify).

NIWC Pacific Office of Small Business Programs deputy director listed in a NAVWAR OSBP brief. CRADA activity in 2025-2026: Public evidence insufficient this session.

organizations.startup_relevance: CRADAs and RAISE onboarding are the technical on-ramp; OSBP is the business on-ramp. ANTX/NICE events accept commercial demonstrations.

organizations.name: Naval Information Warfare Center Atlantic
organizations.portfolio: Charleston, SC; information-warfare engineering, cyber (CSSP), expeditionary/shore C4I; runs the Information Warfare Research Project (IWRP) consortium Other Transaction vehicle with quarterly industry days; partners with the Palmetto Tech Bridge (NIWC Atlantic and Palmetto Tech Bridge Prize Challenge Rodeo, sam.gov d85320522d6a4e95ba2219eb5a288afd).

organizations.startup_relevance: IWRP is the most startup-accessible Navy C2/IW prototype vehicle found: consortium membership plus 'Shark Tank'-style pitch to a NIWC requirement, awarded as prototype OTs. Consortium membership terms and foreign-ownership rules need review.

organizations.portfolio: Navy/Marine Corps innovation facilitation layer (not a contracting office): regional Tech Bridges (Capital/Carderock, Palmetto/Charleston, Pacific, Gulf Coast/Panama City, Northeast/Newport, Southwest and others), prize challenges, industry days (e.g., 'NavalX and DCO UxS Industry Day', 'Carderock Outreach Event - Capital Tech Bridge overview'), Partnership Intermediary Agreements (ONR and NavalX PIA notice on sam.gov).
organizations.current_status_2026: FACT (Tier 4 mirror of FY2025 congressional appropriations tables): Congress added $15.0M for 'NavalX tech bridge facilities' and $5.3M for a 'NavalX regional test and evaluation accelerator' under the Navy Warfighting Experiments and Demonstrations RDT&E line. Gulf Coast Tech Bridge prize challenge fed an ANTX demonstration (DVIDS 465423). Number of Tech Bridges in 2026: Public evidence insufficient.
organizations.startup_relevance: Free, low-friction first contact for a two-founder team; produces introductions to NIWC/NSWC sponsors and prize money, not contracts. Facilitation, not procurement.

organizations.name: Office of Naval Research
organizations.portfolio: Navy and Marine Corps S&T: Long Range BAA (annual), Rapid Fielding Areas of Interest BAA (sam.gov 8c93a97426707052c1e8308cf94db65d), Navy SBIR/STTR program office (navysbir.com; help desk usn.pentagon.cnr-arlington-va.mbx.navy-sbir-sttr@us.navy.mil), NavalX, Naval Research Laboratory, Naval Innovation Science and Engineering (NISE) program funds at warfare centers (general knowledge; not verified this session).
organizations.current_status_2026: FACT (govwin fixture mirror): the DoD SBIR 25.2 BAA ran topics pre-release 2 Apr 2025, open 23 Apr 2025, close 21 May 2025 via DSIP; DON protest rules route through the SYSCOM Program Manager. 2026 cycle specifics: Public evidence insufficient this session.
organizations.startup_relevance: SBIR/STTR (US-owned small business) and the Rapid Fielding BAA are the standard non-dilutive routes; Navy SBIR topics are sponsored by SYSCOMs (NAVWAR, NAVSEA, NAVAIR, MCSC, ONR).

organizations.name: Naval Sea Systems Command / PEO Integrated Warfare Systems
organizations.parent: NAVSEA-affiliated PEO; under PAE Mission Systems since 2026-05-11 (weapons offices IWS 3.0, 11.0, 12.0 moved to PAE Munitions)
organizations.portfolio: Surface combat systems: Aegis and the Integrated Combat System (ICS), radars, EW, undersea sensors, shipboard computing. IWS 6.0 is the combat-system command-and-control and sensor-netting lane (Cooperative Engagement Capability). NAVSEA-approved software factories (The Forge/Black Pearl lineage) deliver afloat/ashore combat-system software; the DoD State of DevSecOps 2025 report cites a NAVSEA team delivering 13 updates to one production-cloud application in nine months.
organizations.current_status_2026: FACT: PEO IWS listed in PAE Mission Systems (11 May 2026). A 'PEO IWS Library, Software, Hardware Asset Reuse Enterprise' notice (sam.gov 87c8f6d04e7809923b74576172209d41) and a 'Mission: Start the Foundry' DevSecOps-sourcing notice (sibling S09) exist. Aegis/ICS 2026 vendor and budget specifics: Public evidence insufficient this session.
organizations.startup_relevance: Combat-system software is safety-critical and prime-dominated (Lockheed Martin Aegis; Raytheon SSDS/CEC, general knowledge); startups enter as subcontractors or through the ICS open-architecture/software-factory notices. Low near-term fit for a two-founder team.

organizations.name: OPNAV resource sponsors and Fleet user commands
organizations.portfolio: OPNAV N2N6 (Information Warfare) is the customary resource sponsor for C4I/ISR/networks (general knowledge; label INFERENCE); N9 sponsors platform combat systems; N8 integrates. Fleet Forces Command and Pacific Fleet Maritime Operations Centers, carrier strike groups and the Naval Information Warfighting Development Center (NIWDC, under Naval Information Forces) generate operational demand and doctrine; the 'Fleet Commander AI Task Force' is cited in the June 2025 Open DAGIR story.
organizations.current_status_2026: INFERENCE: sponsor structure unchanged in public record; the study-guide source flags an OPNAV N3/N5 vs N7 and N8-vs-N9 distinction as current. Specific 2026 N2N6 leadership: Public evidence insufficient.
organizations.leader_title: Deputy CNO for Information Warfare (N2N6); Fleet commanders
key_programs: Requirements for Overmatch, CANES, GCCS-M/MTC2, DCGS-N
organizations.startup_relevance: Operational sponsorship from a Fleet MOC, NIWDC or the Fleet AI task force is what turns a prototype into a funded requirement; startups rarely reach OPNAV directly.

organizations.name: Deputy Commandant for Information
organizations.portfolio: Marine Corps information environment: C5ISR requirements advocacy, Service Data Office (SDO), IC4 (information/C4), AI governance, Marine Corps Software Factory (MCSWF sits within DC I), MCEN policy with PEO Digital.
organizations.current_status_2026: FACT (marines.mil MARADMIN mirrors): LtGen J. A. Matos III signed MARADMIN 135/26 as DC I on 30 Mar 2026 (LtGen Melvin G. Carter held the post in Oct 2024). MCO 5231.4 (11 Mar 2024) established the SDO under DC I; NAVMC 3000.1 USMC AI Implementation Plan approved 23 Apr 2025; MARADMIN 018/26 (21 Jan 2026) makes DC I the centralized approval authority for any GenAI capability (NIPRGPT sunsetting; CamoGPT authorized); MARADMIN 325/26 (21 Jul 2026) announced an Enterprise AI, Data and Software Information Resource Manual.
organizations.leader_title: Deputy Commandant for Information (LtGen J. A. Matos III)
organizations.startup_relevance: Any AI/data/software capability a Marine unit wants to field must clear DC I governance (MARADMIN 018/26); DC I SDO is therefore both gatekeeper and potential champion. MCSWF partnership notices are the concrete door.

organizations.name: Portfolio Acquisition Executive Marine Corps
organizations.portfolio: Single accountable acquisition leader for Marine Corps ground/C5ISR systems; public capability portfolios: C5ISRT, Protect, Sustain/Enable, Maneuver, Fires.
organizations.current_status_2026: FACT (29palms.marines.mil article 4460140, 2026-04-10; pae.marines.mil): formally established 10 Apr 2026; replaced PEO Land Systems and incorporated programs from Marine Corps Systems Command; LtGen Eric Austin holds the dual-hatted PAE role; MCSC became the workforce provider for the Force Development Enterprise. The C5ISRT portfolio is the current home of Marine C2 acquisition (CAC2S, NOTM, MAGTF C2) that previously sat under MCSC's Portfolio Manager Command Element Systems (PfM CES) (legacy label from a Tier 4 org dataset; MEDIUM).
organizations.startup_relevance: C5ISRT portfolio is the buyer for Marine tactical C2 software; contracting still executes through MCSC (M67854; general knowledge). Public 2026 C5ISRT solicitations: Public evidence insufficient this session.

organizations.name: Marine Corps Systems Command
organizations.parent: Commandant of the Marine Corps (SYSCOM); programs realigned to PAE-MC
organizations.portfolio: Contracting, engineering, test (MCTSSA) and workforce support for Marine acquisition; legacy portfolio managers PfM Command Element Systems and PfM Ground Combat Element Systems; Marine Corps Tactical Systems Support Activity (MCTSSA, Camp Pendleton) provides test, evaluation, TAK training and tactical-systems support.
organizations.current_status_2026: FACT (2026-04-10 release): MCSC assumed an expanded role as workforce provider for the Force Development Enterprise while programs moved under PAE-MC. MCTSSA collaborations with MCSWF and the Marine Innovation Unit continued through 2025-2026 (Marine Coders articles 2025-03-30, 2025-09-20, 2025-11-22).
key_programs: Handheld Radio Test Set (IOC May 2025, DVIDS 501138)
organizations.startup_relevance: Contracting execution point and technical gate (MCTSSA interoperability testing) for anything sold into Marine C2; MCTSSA is also the TAK-plugin integration hub for Marine tactical edge apps.

organizations.name: Marine Corps Software Factory
organizations.portfolio: Austin, TX organic software development: trains Marines as product managers, developers and UI/UX designers in three-year tours, then reassigns teams to MEF Information Group (MIG) commanders; product portfolio includes TAK plugins (ARES helicopter-landing-zone predictor, Flight Mode), Reserve Hub, and CRUSADER (government-built software to control commercial radars for tactical use). Founded on the Army Software Factory model by LtCol Charlie Bahk; championed by then-DC I LtGen Glavy.
organizations.current_status_2026: FACT (Marine Coders/MIU articles): sprints with the Marine Innovation Unit and MCTSSA in June 2024, March 2025 (36 personnel), September 2025 (14 coders), planning 2026 engagements at MIU training Nov 2025; a 'Marine Corps Software Factory - Notice of Intent' was posted on sam.gov (21370260a9ca4f9bbcc4c671d346b5b9). Marine Corps Gazette (Oct 2025) argues for software engineers at the tactical edge via MIU/MCSWF.
organizations.startup_relevance: MCSWF builds in-house and 'welcomes partnering'; a startup fits as a tooling/platform or TAK-plugin partner, not as an app vendor competing with organic teams. TAK ecosystem is the shared substrate (TAK Offsite 2025).

organizations.name: Marine Corps Warfighting Laboratory / Combat Development and Integration
organizations.parent: Deputy Commandant for Combat Development and Integration (MCCDC)
organizations.portfolio: Force Design experimentation; identifies and matures new capabilities; Marine Requirements Oversight Council process sits with CD&I. MCWL contracts directly (FAR RDT&E) and via consortium OTAs (Advanced Technology International-managed vehicles).
organizations.current_status_2026: FACT (sibling company batches, MEDIUM): MCWL awarded Reveal Technology a $3.2M RDT&E contract to enhance Farsight (edge 3D mapping) and pursued a common controller for tactical robotic systems (Tomahawk product line) through an ATI-managed consortium. 2026 experiment campaign specifics for C2: Public evidence insufficient this session.
organizations.leader_title: Commanding General, MCWL (Brig. Gen.); Deputy Commandant CD&I (LtGen)
organizations.startup_relevance: Most startup-friendly Marine buyer found: small FAR RDT&E awards and consortium OTAs for edge software with an experimentation sponsor.

organizations.name: Chief Digital and AI Office and Defense Innovation Unit (as Navy on-ramps)
organizations.portfolio: Open DAGIR pipeline and Maven Smart System hosting; DIU Commercial Solutions Openings with a Navy sponsor.
organizations.current_status_2026: FACT (DVIDS 501030, 2025-06-18): Project Overmatch, NAVWAR, CDAO and DIU jointly onboarded commercial AI/ML applications through Open DAGIR for Fleet commanders. Sibling joint.json: Maven Smart System designated CJADC2 cornerstone (Apr 2026) with Marine Corps among users.
organizations.leader_title: Chief Digital and AI Officer; Director, DIU
organizations.startup_relevance: A Navy-sponsored DIU CSO or Open DAGIR onboarding is currently the most credible way for a commercial software product to reach Overmatch without a classified track record.

programs.name: Project Overmatch (Naval Operational Architecture)
programs.owner: DRPM Overmatch under PAE Mission Systems (PM Capt. Remil Capili); NAVWAR/NIWC Pacific technical execution
programs.description: Navy CJADC2 contribution: resilient networks, data architecture and cloud analytics linking manned and unmanned platforms; Overmatch Software Armory for DevSecOps; Five Eyes coalition integration. Started 2020 under then-Rear Adm. Doug Small.
programs.status_2026: Deployed to three carrier strike groups by Mar 2024; Five Eyes Project Arrangement (announced 2025); coalition lab and RIMPAC 2026 testing; Open DAGIR commercial AI onboarding (June 2025); spending planned through FY2029 (Tier 4). Rolling fielding, not complete.
vendors: Palantir (Maven Smart System via CDAO/Open DAGIR - FACT)
Ocean Power Technologies (participation, no definitive award - Tier 4 10-K)

contract_evidence.vehicle: FY2025 appropriations increase 'ATRT for Project Overmatch' (Automated Test and Re-Test line)

budget.pe_number_or_line: Public evidence insufficient: Overmatch funding is spread across NAVWAR RDT&E lines and largely non-public; FY2024 request reported as $192M (C4ISRNET).

programs.third_party_software_openness: Medium in principle, low in practice: OSA/RAISE lets containerized third-party apps inherit the platform ATO, and Open DAGIR onboarded commercial AI apps in 2025; but the architecture is classified and participation is by sponsor invitation. A NAVWAR 'Project Overmatch Prize Challenge' (historical, navy.mil) shows prize-based entry has been used.

programs.name: Overmatch Software Armory (OSA)
programs.owner: NIWC Pacific (host) / PEO Digital (management per NPS thesis) / DRPM Overmatch
programs.description: Navy cloud-enabled DevSecOps ecosystem: OSA Tools, Agile Core Services, Collaborative Staging Environments, Application Arsenal; RAISE continuous accreditation; secret-level environment launched 2021.
programs.status_2026: Operating; designated RAISE Platform of Choice under the RAISE 2.0 Implementation Guide (v1.0, 4 Oct 2022, DON CIO). NAVADMIN 342/20 made the OSA pipeline available for CANES-hosted applications. 2026 throughput metrics: Public evidence insufficient.
vendors: Public evidence insufficient (platform tooling vendors not identified)
programs.third_party_software_openness: High for accredited containers: RAISE 2.0 defines 8 security gates (SAST, SBOM, secrets, container scan, DAST, ISSM review, signing, registry) and lets an application owner incorporate into the RPOC ATO instead of obtaining a standalone ATO; residual risk must not exceed Moderate; High findings remediated within 21 days.

programs.name: Consolidated Afloat Networks and Enterprise Services (CANES)
programs.description: Shipboard network, compute, enterprise services and cybersecurity infrastructure hosting C2 and mission applications; ACAT IAC/IAM; sustained by COTS refresh and service packs.
programs.status_2026: In production/fielding and modernization (PMW 160 tear sheet 2025-01-31). Hosts applications from PMW 120/150; OSA pipeline available for CANES apps.
vendors: BAE Systems (2022 award cited as $4.1B by NPS thesis; likely a multiple-award IDIQ ceiling, not revenue - LOW/MEDIUM)
Other CANES production awardees: Public evidence insufficient this session

contract_evidence.ceiling: $4.1B (as stated by NPS thesis; treat as ceiling)

budget.pe_number_or_line: PE 0303138N Consolidated Afloat Networks and Enterprise Services (RDT&E; PE code existence confirmed in a congressional line-item dataset; title from general knowledge - MEDIUM) plus OPN procurement line

programs.third_party_software_openness: Hosting platform: third-party apps run on CANES only after accreditation (RAISE/OSA route) and PMW 160 configuration control; startups do not sell 'to' CANES but must be CANES-compatible.

programs.name: Automated Digital Network System (ADNS)
programs.description: Tactical WAN and ship-to-shore IP routing/traffic engineering layer between CANES and SATCOM/RF bearers.
programs.status_2026: Sustainment/modernization; details: Public evidence insufficient this session.
programs.third_party_software_openness: Low; network-layer program dominated by integrators.

programs.name: GCCS-M / Maritime Tactical Command and Control (MTC2)
programs.owner: PEO C4I PMW 150 Naval Command and Control Systems
programs.description: Navy operational/tactical C2 applications: common operational/tactical picture, commander's picture, planning and decision support; MTC2 is the web-services successor to GCCS-M; PMW 150 also owns C2P and Link 16 network modernization on ships.
programs.status_2026: Active (PMW 150 tear sheet, January 2026). MTC2 fielding status and vendors: Public evidence insufficient this session.

budget.pe_number_or_line: PE 0604231N Tactical Command System (PE code existence confirmed in a congressional dataset; title from general knowledge - MEDIUM)

programs.third_party_software_openness: Medium: MTC2's service-oriented design is intended to host third-party widgets/services (general knowledge; verify), and PMW 150 is the natural integration owner for any COP/decision-support app.

programs.name: DCGS-N / Intelligence Carry-On Program (ICOP)
programs.owner: PEO C4I PMW 120 Battlespace Awareness and Information Operations
programs.description: Afloat/ashore ISR processing, exploitation and dissemination; migrating from hardware-heavy deployments to afloat and ashore cloud environments; ICOP extends DCGS-N to smaller units.
programs.status_2026: Cloud-transition strategy stated in a study-guide reference (MEDIUM); PMW 120 overview tear sheet dated 2026-02-25. Vendors and budget: Public evidence insufficient this session.
programs.third_party_software_openness: Medium: the program's stated strategy is 'more rapid integration of third-party analytical tools' in cloud environments; the strongest PEO C4I fit for an ISR analytics startup.

programs.name: DJC2 / Maritime Operations Center (MOC) / Shore Tactical Assured C2 (STACC)
programs.owner: PEO C4I PMW 790 Shore and Expeditionary Integration
programs.description: Deployable Joint Command and Control (ACAT IAC), the MOC project coordinating delivery of more than 100 C4ISR capabilities to Fleet commanders, and the STACC shore C2 portfolio with its own DevSecOps pipeline (NAVADMIN 342/20 said STACC pipeline online summer 2021).

procurement_pathways.how_it_works_here: Navy SBIR/STTR is run by ONR with topics sponsored by NAVWAR, NAVSEA, NAVAIR, MCSC and ONR; proposals go through the DoD DSIP portal on the DoD-wide BAA cycle (25.2 cycle: pre-release 2 Apr 2025, open 23 Apr, close 21 May 2025). Phase II awards in the low seven figures (example: Navy SBIR Phase II N68335-23-C-0585, $1,658,607, NAVAIR, 2023 - sibling B02). CAC2S AI-assistant topic was awarded to Leverege.
procurement_pathways.typical_award_size: Phase I ~$140K-$250K; Phase II ~$1M-$2M (general Navy norms; verify current BAA)
procurement_pathways.timeline: Three cycles per year; ~6 months from topic release to Phase I award; Phase II 24 months

how_a_startup_gets_in: Sequenced plan grounded in the offices/events found (all dates should be re-verified at source). (1) Months 0-3, no-cost discovery: register in SAM; email the NAVWAR Small Business Office (navwarsbo.fct@navy.mil) and NIWC Pacific/Atlantic OSBP; attend a NavalX Tech Bridge outreach (Capital Tech Bridge/Carderock, Palmetto/Charleston, Pacific/San Diego) and the PEO Digital PMW 270 Quarterly Industry Engagement; join the IWRP consortium and attend its quarterly industry day to see NIWC Atlantic requirements (e.g., NEWT-style edge terminals). (2) Months 3-9, demonstrate: enter a NavalX/Tech Bridge prize challenge or the NICE CSO/ANTX cycle with a working software prototype; pursue a NIWC CRADA to get the product into a lab; if U.S.-ownership rules can be met, submit to the next Navy SBIR cycle on a NAVWAR- or MCSC-sponsored C2/ISR topic (25.2 timing: pre-release early April, close late May). (3) Months 6-18, first dollars: pitch an IWRP prototype OT against a NIWC requirement; respond to OTA-eligible sources-sought notices (e.g., 'Navy Collaborative' 2026-08-31, TacMobile Inc 3); for Marine edge software, engage MCWL (small FAR RDT&E awards like the $3.2M Farsight contract) and the Marine Corps Software Factory/MCTSSA as a TAK-plugin partner, clearing DC I governance early if any AI is involved (MARADMIN 018/26). (4) Months 12-24, path to Overmatch: containerize and push through the Overmatch Software Armory/RAISE 2.0 gates (SAST, SBOM, secrets, container scan, DAST, ISSM review, signing, registry) to inherit the platform ATO; seek a Navy-sponsored DIU CSO or Open DAGIR onboarding through CDAO; or subcontract to an integrator with Overmatch access. (5) Structural prerequisites to resolve in parallel with counsel: SBIR/STTR U.S.-ownership thresholds versus a German permanent-resident founder and an Indonesian non-U.S. founder; FOCI mitigation and facility clearance if any classified integration is required (Overmatch is largely Secret); ITAR/EAR classification of the product; CMMC readiness for CUI. Signals to watch: PAE Mission Systems and PAE Marine Corps industry days (new in 2026), MUSV-style PAE marketplaces spreading to mission systems, and the FY2027 justification books for Overmatch/CANES/CAC2S lines.

saturation_statement: Not saturated. Coverage is strong on 2026 organizational structure (PAE reorganization of Mar-May 2026, DRPM Overmatch, PAE Marine Corps, DC I governance) because a well-sourced mirror of official releases was reachable, and adequate on pathways (IWRP, NICE CSO, NavalX, SBIR, MCWL, MCSWF). Coverage is weak on: current NAVWAR, PEO C4I and PEO Digital leaders; FY2026/FY2027 program-element dollar values for Overmatch, CANES, ADNS, DCGS-N, MCEN and CAC2S; named Overmatch vendors and any obligated contract values; NIWC CRADA and ANTX 2025-2026 specifics; Navy SBIR 26.x C2 topics; Aegis/ICS 2026 software contracting. Every item marked 'Public evidence insufficient' is a direct consequence of the blocked web access described in access_constraints_note, not evidence of absence. A follow-up pass with working WebSearch/WebFetch should prioritize comptroller.defense.gov FY2027 RDT&E N and PMC justification books, peoc4i.navy.mil leadership/tear-sheet pages, navwar.navy.mil leadership, sam.gov IWRP/NICE/PMW 270 notices, and the GAO-25-106454 Defense Command and Control report.
